checks: Eight unique static views captured from this clean main-derived WebGPU build; authored solar assets loaded.

scenes.name: high-orbit-direct-36000km-atmosphere-on
scenes.review: The disk silhouette is clear, but long-range radial spokes are prominent, regular and compete with the halo/corona. The core is clipped white at exposure 1; highlight roll-off is not demonstrated.

scenes.name: high-orbit-limb-36000km-atmosphere-on
scenes.review: The Sun is framed above the Earth limb, but a narrow saturated cyan/yellow edge follows the silhouette and reads as a hard rim. Source attribution is still required.

scenes.name: low-orbit-sunrise-400km-atmosphere-on
scenes.review: Orbital sunrise geometry is legible, but the red/orange horizon band is strongly saturated and radial artwork remains conspicuous.

scenes.name: low-orbit-low-sun-400km-atmosphere-on
scenes.review: The warm horizon band and radial rays dominate; physical transport and Bloom contributions need to be separated using existing matched controls.

scenes.name: near-ground-low-sun-2km-atmosphere-on
scenes.review: The broad pale warm sky washes out the view and the Sun reads as a small, low-contrast disk.

scenes.name: ground-day-2m-atmosphere-on
scenes.review: The daytime disk remains visible with a smooth bounded glow and no obvious hard halo boundary in this frame; fine corona/rays are naturally subdued at this scale.

scenes.name: ground-twilight-2m-atmosphere-on
scenes.review: The yellow field is nearly uniform and disk contrast is weak. Existing physical-only/no-Bloom baseline controls show much of the yellow predates B4 artwork integration.

scenes.name: ground-night-2m-atmosphere-on
scenes.review: No obvious solar-artwork residual is visible, but the constant-color unlit night-side surface remains bright blue and prevents a complete ground-night scene judgement.
